headline: Revenue climbs, but fuel and labor costs squeeze margins
summary_short: United reported Q2 2026 revenue of $17,672M (+16.0% y/y) as passenger revenue rose 16.4% on higher yields and traffic, but a 84.1% y/y jump in aircraft fuel expense cut operating income to $1,096M (-17.3% y/y) and net income to $805M (-17.3% y/y, $2.48 basic EPS).
summary_long: Revenue rose 16.0% y/y to $17,672M, led by a $2.3B (16.4%) rise in passenger revenue on a 12.1% yield gain and 5.4% more passengers, plus cargo +22.6%. Operating expense rose 19.2% y/y to $16,576M, driven by aircraft fuel (+84.1% y/y) and a 6.2% rise in salaries from a new flight-attendant labor deal. Operating income fell 17.3% y/y to $1,096M and net income fell 17.3% to $805M ($2.48 basic / $2.46 diluted EPS); a $181M AFA ratification charge was mostly offset by $351M of sale-leaseback gains. Cash and short-term investments reached $16.6B, up from $12.2B at 2025 year-end, on $5.8B of debt issuance and $6.4B of operating cash flow against $3.0B of capex. No forward guidance is in this 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth was outpaced by a fuel-cost surge tied to Middle East geopolitical disruption; management says it took capacity and fare actions to mitigate, and remains confident in demand longer-term.
Passenger revenue rose 16.4% y/y on a 12.1% yield increase and 5.4% more passengers flown; cargo revenue rose 22.6% on higher freight yields.

Total operating expense rose 19.2% y/y, primarily aircraft fuel expense +84.1% on higher per-gallon price and consumption, plus a 6.2% rise in salaries from higher headcount and a new flight-attendant pay agreement.
This shard figure is numerically identical to ebitda_usd_m across all periods and is not itself discussed in the filing's narrative; tracks the same fuel-driven operating-income decline.
Not explained in the release — this Yahoo-derived figure does not correspond to any line item United itself discloses (airlines report no distinct COGS line).

Net income fell y/y on the fuel and labor cost increases described above, though a $181M flight-attendant ratification charge was largely offset by $351M of aircraft sale-leaseback gains, leaving net special items a $156M credit versus a $293M charge a year ago.
Tracks the same operating-income decline as net income; nonoperating expense, net was roughly flat y/y ($69M vs $77M).
EPS declined in line with net income; weighted diluted shares were roughly flat y/y (-0.2%), so per-share moves closely track the net-income decline.

Cash and short-term investments rose to $16.6B from $12.2B at 2025 year-end, funded by $5.8B of debt issuance (including $1.0B 5.375% notes due 2031 and $1.0B 4.875% notes due 2029) and $6.4B of operating cash flow, against $4.5B of debt repayments and $3.0B of capex.
Not explained in the release beyond the overall liquidity build described for total cash.
Equity growth is consistent with $805M of quarterly net income accreting to retained earnings, partially offset by $27M of share repurchases this quarter.
Share count held roughly flat as minimal repurchase activity (no buybacks in Q2 itself) was offset by shares issued for share-based awards.
